title: Scale: Storage Fabric, Migratable Job, and worker placement
summary: Process bounded video chunks on 8–16 eligible CPU workers when available; GPU is an optional placement capability. Storage Fabric carries durable source and checkpoint references, Migratable Job handles continuation, and Job-to-Node Allocation handles eligibility, leases and fencing.
invariants: Never turn clip/job IDs into assumed Storage Fabric object IDs before object pinning is confirmed.
Never put large video payloads in queue messages; carry stable references, hashes, time windows and evidence only.
Chunk boundaries are half-open PTS intervals; any tracking overlap must be explicitly recorded and de-duplicated during history reconciliation.
History blocks can associate face/pose observation tracks across time without declaring true human identity.
Multi-face MediaPipe Face Landmarker and Pose Landmarker are target capabilities; actual MediaPipe inference on A02 is not yet qualified.
ZeroGPU and Colab are opportunistic execution destinations, not assured permanent unattended mesh workers.
procedure: Pin source video and model versions in Storage Fabric.
Create bounded, checkpointable work definitions; use existing node placement authority and migratable job leases.
Workers run Face Landmarker or Pose Landmarker via Foreign Runtime/compatible Python provider.
Write atomic, integrity-verifiable outputs; reconcile observations in source-PTS order.
Checkpoint all future-determining continuation state and avoid duplicate result promotion after migration.

provenance.claim: FFmpeg PTS range tracking and checkpoint interface, with MediaPipe not runtime-qualified.
Independent timestamped transcription gateway and local face-analysis seam.
